def: Software-set upper bound on the data rate a port will try to reach in link training; combined with Retrain Link to change speed. It is a cap, not the current speed (Link Status shows that).
A CPU memory type in which stores are buffered and merged into larger writes that may leave the CPU out of program order; useful for bulk MMIO such as CMB submission queues, never for doorbells.
A small field (in the MSI-X capability, CMBLOC, PMRCAP and similar) that names which BAR holds a structure; an index, used with an offset, not an address.

Declares that reads of a memory BAR's region have no side effects and writes may be merged, allowing prefetching and placement in a bridge's (possibly 64-bit) prefetchable window. It does not set the CPU memory type.
A capability listing the sizes a BAR supports and letting software choose one before the BAR is assigned.
The two bits preceding each 128-bit block on a lane at 8.0-32.0 GT/s, marking a data block or an ordered-set block; 00b and 11b are invalid and are reported as receiver errors.
Ordered set sent at a scheduled interval on all lanes whose SKP symbols receivers may add or remove in their elastic buffers to compensate for clock-rate differences.
Receiver buffer crossing from the recovered clock to the local clock; it adds or removes SKP symbols to absorb frequency differences. Overflow or underflow is a receiver error.

exp: Separate Reference clocks with Independent Spread spectrum clocking
def: Clocking architecture in which each end of a link has its own reference clock with spread spectrum enabled; requires more frequent SKP ordered sets and must be configured at both ends.

The LTSSM state that re-establishes lock and agreement on a working link, and through which speed changes, equalization, width changes and L1 exits pass. Usually normal; frequent error-driven entries are not.

Data Link Layer state reached after flow-control initialization (InitFC1/InitFC2) completes on a trained link; TLPs may flow only in this state. Reported as Data Link Layer Link Active in Link Status where supported.
Deeper low-power substates of link state L1 in which common-mode voltage and the reference clock may be removed, coordinated through CLKREQ#; exit is slower than from L1.0.
AER correctable error reported by a port that could not decode what it received: 8b/10b code or disparity errors, invalid sync headers, framing errors, elastic-buffer over/underflow.
A Physical Layer device that fully receives and retransmits the signal, participates in link training and splits the channel into separately equalized segments; up to two per link.
Per-rate, per-direction tuning of transmitter coefficients (and receiver adaptation) at 8 GT/s and above, in Phases 0-3, with results recorded in status registers.
